newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Barea says spending cut to be 800 bln ptas.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Barea says spending cut to be 800 bln ptas.

text.p: The Spanish government will cut spending by 800 billion pesetas to meet 1997 European convergence criteria for the public deficit, budget office director Jose Barea said on Tuesday.
"Spending will be reduced by around two percent compared with the final budget for this year," Barea told journalists after a parliamentary commission budget meeting.
The 1997 budget is to be presented to parliament before the end of September.
He detailed a freeze in public sector pay and a 10-percent fall in purchases of goods and service, which together will save a total 220.23 billion pesetas.
A cut in public investment will reduce expenditure by 100-150 billion pesetas.
A cut in subsidies to public companies will total 150-200 billion pesetas, Barea said.
